findings.title: `website_name` bypasses TL0 profile-field restrictions
findings.body: `website_name` is serialized independently of `website`, but it is not included in `untrusted_attributes`. For anonymous views of a TL0 user, `include_website?` suppresses the actual website while this new attribute still exposes its hostname and, for matching instance domains, its full path. This defeats the existing privacy restriction for the website profile field. Apply the same restriction to `website_name` (or make its inclusion depend on `include_website?`) and add coverage for an anonymous TL0 serialization.

findings.title: Website-name inclusion predicate has the wrong serializer method name
findings.body: The serializer convention used throughout this class is `include_<attribute>?` (for example `include_card_image_badge_id?`). This method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel serialization will not use it as the inclusion predicate. Consequently `website_name` is treated as an unconditional attribute and can be emitted as null for present-but-unparseable website values; more importantly, the intended guard is not actually enforcing any visibility policy. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and make that predicate honor the website visibility restriction.
